purpose: Measured baseline batch for Beta1 contextual-review throughput; no throughput optimization experiment was mixed into the review.

timing.timing_note: Reading was stopwatch-measured from the start to end of the direct JP -> pinned EN -> KO read. Edit drafting was separately timed while finalizing the 28 replacement strings. Evidence time is the explicitly phase-timed manifest/queue/scope construction work and includes connector latency inside those phase boundaries. ci_wait_seconds counts only the two successful final jobs (heavy 43s + final scope 26s), matching the normalized convention used by throughput-021. incident_seconds is the 19s deliberate placeholder packet-hash discovery run; it was process overhead, not a translation/runtime failure. The remaining 93.0s is left explicitly unattributed rather than invented as active review time; it includes branch/file checks, hash sealing, commit/API round trips and other connector/wait overhead within the wall-clock window.

derived_baseline.warning: Do not extrapolate this single batch to the whole remaining corpus. Batch 022 is materially easier than Batch 021 by edit rate (20.9% versus 50.8%) and contains many short location/item/equipment rows. This is the first measured baseline, not an authoritative corpus ETA.

scope_hash_discovery.reason: Deliberate zero-hash mismatch used only to obtain the CI-reconstructed deterministic packet SHA; no ledger/coverage mutation occurred.
